page.layout: One column of running text. Marginal notes stand in the right margin beside the text. Running head at top left, page number at top right. Gathering signature and catchword at the foot.

main_text.l: nos scribit: pro virili prouehere eadem cu-
pere: non tamen agnoscere prudentiam,
doctrinam, usum rerum atque experien-
tiam, vel alia quæ amicus nobis tribuat:
esse ipsum talem, ut nostro, vel aliorum o-
pus consilio non habeat: aut liberum re-
linquere amico, ut quod optimum videa-
tur faciat: gratum fore, si, quod suademus,
approbarit: non molestum, si aliud secu-
tus fuerit. Sed neque mouentes sunt sen-
tentiæ negligendæ, verùm petendæ vel à
ipse & confidentia: vel metu ac reformida-
tione: vel æmulatione, quæ in erectis &
generosis maximè animis locum haber:
ut ipes aut metus in reliquis. Ad tracta-
tionem verò atque collocationem quod
attinet: aliter ea est instituenda, cùm quid
faciendum nobis aut intermittendum
videatur ostendimus: aliter cùm in medio
deliberationem atque consultationem
relinquimus, & suspendimus iudicium.
Cum sententiam explicamus nostram: ac
probamus aliquid, aut improbamus: pri-
ma erit pars Exordium, constans, aut [illegible, ~4 letters]-
[illegible, ~8 letters] repetitione acceptarum literarum.
libro quinto, epistol. 19. libro sexto, epist.
8. Aut commendatione & laude amoris,
benevolentiæ, humanitatis amici.

page.notes: Greek word in the paragraph beginning "Cum sententiam" is partly illegible; the printed Greek after "aut" is unreadable on the scan. Running head converted u to U in capitals per the rules. Catchword "libro" sits on the last printed line; I have treated it as a catchword rather than text. The page number reads as "81" (printed with a dotless-i style numeral). The note "Momentes" and "sententiæ." are two printed notes at the same position, kept as separate notes.
